title: Fix Puzzle 3D Introduction Steps Not Revealing Folded Anchors
description: Puzzle 3D's first-run introduction walkthrough (framework Introduction mechanism) fails from step 3 onward: "Move Objects" (step 3, anchors on the "move" utility), "The Catalogue" (step 4, anchors on the catalogue panel tab), and "Add an Object" (step 5, anchors on the addObjectKind action) all render as a centered box with no highlighted cutout, because their DOM anchors are inside chrome that's folded/closed by default (the window Tools toolbar, the "transform" utility sub-group picker, the dock panel containing the Catalogue tab, and the Actions rail). The introduction system (ui/js/react/index.tsx useIntroductionAnchorRect) only polls for the anchor's mount via a CSS selector — it never opens the containers that would make it mount. Root-cause fix: when the active introduction step changes, the shell must reveal whatever chrome contains that step's anchor (unfold the toolbar / expand the utility's sub-group / open the dock panel + select its tab / unfold the Actions rail) before/while the anchor rect is measured, using the existing per-window fold and per-anchor panel-visibility state (extending it to the toolbar, which today is uncontrolled local state on Window unlike the Actions rail which already has controlled fold state in shellState.actionPane). Verify live via the puzzle-3d-react-dev preview by stepping through steps 1-5 of the intro and confirming each one highlights and lets the user complete it.
